messages:
alice: Preparing to apply infra changes for release 2026-03-20. Targeting us-west-2 primary, canary in eu-west-1. Change window 23:00-00:30 UTC. Plan posted below. /cc @infra-oncall @carol

deploy-bot: terraform plan for branch release/2026-03-20
```
# summary: 3 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy
+ aws_iam_role.redwood_service (new)
~ aws_route_table.rw (modify tags)
+ aws_lb_target_group.canary (new)
```
Plan: https://deploy.redwood.internal/plans/abc123

bob: what's the provider pin? last time provider upgrade caused diff noise.

carol: pinning to `hashicorp/aws v4.65.0` in providers.tf. confirm in PR.

alice: confirmed. provider pinned and lockfile updated. Will run `terraform init -upgrade=false` during apply.

infra-oncall: IAM role creation needs approval. Are policies reviewed? last-minute wide-scoped policy blocked me during previous run.

alice: policies are scoped, added explicit actions + resource ARNs. See snippet:
```
resource "aws_iam_policy" "svc_write" {
  name = "svc-write-${var.release}"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [{ Action = ["s3:PutObject"], Resource = "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod/*", Effect = "Allow" }]
  })
}
```

dave: Can we canary the target group in eu-west-1 only (5% traffic) and rollback to previous TG if health fails? How do we flip traffic?

carol: Use the routing canary in the Load Balancer config + Route53 weighted records. Plan includes `aws_lb_listener_rule` update and `aws_route53_record` weighted set.

deploy-bot: Starting serial apply (canary eu-west-1) at 2026-03-20T23:05:00Z. Change window ends 2026-03-20T00:30:00Z. Apply ID: apply-xyz789

alice: monitoring: dashboards -> /dashboards/release/2026-03-20 . Alerts: target-response-time and 5xx rate.

bob: If canary health < 90% for 5m, we rollback. Rollback playbook is https://runbook.internal/rollback/infra-apply

infra-oncall: manual approval required before cross-account role creation. I approved in prism (ticket #INC-4221) :white_check_mark:

carol: apply output shows new role ARN: arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood_service_2026-03-20

deploy-bot: Apply completed in eu-west-1 (canary): success. 1 resource added, 1 changed. Health checks passing.

alice: proceeding to staged rollouts in us-west-2 -> us-east-1 with 10min pause between regions.

dave: tagging rollback window in case we need to revert: `terraform state rm` won't restore old TG; we'll point Route53 back to previous target group id. Keep previous TG id from state.

bob: also keep the previous ALB listener rule id in case we need to revert. I pushed a small script `tools/safe-roll.sh` to repo.

alice: us-west-2 apply started.

deploy-bot: Apply failed in us-west-2: error creating aws_lb_target_group.canary: InvalidPort: Port '0' is not valid

alice: ack. rolling back last region and reverting Route53 weight to 100% previous. Initiating rollback now.

carol: quick note: bug in module default port variable. Patch in PR #487 fixes default to 8080. We'll cherry-pick to hotfix branch after rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed: Route53 weights restored, target group deleted. Apply aborted for remaining regions.

infra-oncall: Incident ticket created: INC-4230. Leaving change window open until we confirm hotfix. :warning:

alice: Postmortem next steps: 1) backport module change + validation in TF plan CI 2) add port validation check in the module 3) schedule a new apply outside blackout. I'll add notes to release: https://redwood.example.com/releases/2026-03-20#infra

dave: thumbs up. small followups: add `preflight` step to deploy-bot that runs a dry-run on module defaults.

bob: Agree. Also add provider lock check: fail apply if `providers.tf` uses unpinned version.

alice: Thanks all. Closing this thread once hotfix cherry-pick merged. :party-parrot:
